title: LockLab reviews: pill, cost, guarantee and FutureClinic - FutureClinic
summary: LockLab reviews: 6-in-1 pill doses, side effects, $35 to $52/mo on 3- or 5-month plans (Nov 2026), 365-day guarantee terms, BBB grade, and FutureClinic.
body_markdown:
LockLab's 6-in-1 pill combines oral minoxidil 5 mg and finasteride 1.1 mg with vitamins and zinc; the 7-in-1 adds dutasteride 0.1 mg ($35 to $52/month on 3- or 5-month plans, November 2026). A FutureClinic dermatologist can instead[prescribe FDA-approved generics by message, with no subscription](https://futureclinic.com/blog/hair-loss-treatment-online-without-a-subscription) .


## Is LockLab legit?


LockLab is Lock Lab, LLC in Delaware ([Terms & Conditions](https://www.locklab.co/terms-conditions) ), founded by David DiMuzio and Dr. Dan McGrath ([Our Story](https://www.locklab.co/our-story) ). Its terms state it does not practice medicine; its[Telehealth Consent](https://www.locklab.co/telehealth-consent) calls it a management services organization whose medical groups use physicians, nurse practitioners and physician assistants (you may request a physician). Per the[FAQ](https://www.locklab.co/faq) , a provider reviews a 2-minute questionnaire within 24 hours (replies typically take 12 hours), with no visit. The FAQ says 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico;[Medical Experts](https://www.locklab.co/medical-experts) says 49 states and D.C., excluding Alabama.


## What is in the LockLab pill?


LockLab's 6-in-1 contains oral minoxidil 5 mg, finasteride 1.1 mg, biotin 1 mg, D3 2,000 IU, B3 16 mg and zinc 10 mg, compounded at Partell Pharmacy in Las Vegas; the 7-in-1 adds dutasteride 0.1 mg ([The Science](https://www.locklab.co/the-science) ,[Pricing](https://www.locklab.co/pricing) ). LockLab also offers[Custom Rx](https://www.locklab.co/custom-rx) and[LockLab Women](https://www.locklab.co/women) . Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Finasteride is[FDA-approved for male hair loss](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=finasteride) at 1 mg daily (LockLab uses 1.1 mg);[oral minoxidil](https://www.locklab.co/the-science) and[dutasteride](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=dutasteride) are off-label. In a[2024 trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38598226/) and[2025 meta-analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39425514/) , oral minoxidil matched topical minoxidil for density, with extra body hair twice as common. The[AAD](https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/hair-loss/treatment/diagnosis-treat) advises taking biotin, iron or zinc only when a blood test shows a deficiency, and the[FDA](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/in-vitro-diagnostics/biotin-interference-troponin-lab-tests-assays-subject-biotin-interference) warns biotin skews labs.


## What do LockLab reviews and ratings show?


As of November 2026, the[Better Business Bureau (BBB)](https://www.bbb.org/search?find_text=lock%20lab&find_country=USA) gives Lock Lab LLC a B+ grade (not BBB accredited). LockLab's Medical Experts page states an "Average 5-star rating" without naming a site, and its[homepage](https://www.locklab.co/) marks stories "Verified review" without naming a verifier.


## What are the side effects of LockLab's ingredients?


On the finasteride 1 mg label, year-one sexual side effects occurred in 3.8% of men versus 2.1% on placebo (decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, ejaculation disorder); post-marketing reports add persistent sexual effects, breast changes, testicular pain, infertility, and depression or suicidal thoughts. A[2026 review](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41118052/) of low-dose oral minoxidil reports extra facial or body hair in 24%, temporary shedding in 16% to 22%, and mild swelling in 2%. LockLab's FAQ warns against use with low blood pressure or blood-pressure drugs; its[drug page](https://www.locklab.co/drug-info/locklab) lists dizziness, fast heartbeat, chest pain, shortness of breath, swelling, and "a rare chance of pericardial effusion". Finasteride and dutasteride in the[7-in-1](https://www.locklab.co/drug-info/locklab-dutasteride) (5-week half-life) lower PSA, bar blood donation (6 months for dutasteride, per[the dutasteride label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=dutasteride) ), and must not be handled by women who are or could become pregnant.


## What does LockLab cost, and how does the 365-day guarantee work?


As of November 2026, LockLab's 6-in-1 costs $35/month on a 5-month plan ($175) or $47/month on a 3-month plan; the 7-in-1 is $39/month on a 5-month plan ($195; $49 struck to $39 on the homepage, as a limited-time offer for checkout before 12/31) or $52/month on a 3-month plan. Terms list an $80 monthly plan; Custom Rx starts at $45/month and LockLab Women at $39/month (November 2026). Shipping and messaging are included; insurance is not accepted (FSA/HSA cards are). Plans auto-renew up to 15 days early on the first refill and 2 days early later; cancel at least 24 hours before renewal, with no part-period refunds except case by case.


From September 17, 2026 (terms vary by enrollment date), men's 3- and 5-month plans refund first-year payments if you finish 365 days and "do not see results". You must upload baseline photos within 14 days and photos at days 180 and 270, keep an unbroken 365-day subscription without pausing or stopping for side effects without approval, and apply between day 365 and 395. A provider grades day-365 photos; if the pill "stabilized the condition or halted further progression," the guarantee is void.
